senses.gloss: Kauśala (III, 2897), v. Kosala.
Kauśala, pl. (ºāḥ), (VII, 397), v. Kosala, pl.
Kauśalya, Kauśalya, pl., Kauśalyā, Kauśalyānandavardhana, Kauśalyānandivardhana, Kauśalyāmatṛ, Kauśalyātmajā, v. Kausº.

Kausalya^1 (C. Kauśº) (“the king of the Kosalas”) = Bṛhadbala: V, 5765 (Bº); VI, 623 (Bº, only in B., C. has by error Kauravyaḥ), 3534 (Bº), 3855 (Bº), 5325 (Bº), 5408; VII, 1964 (has been slain by Abhimanyu), 2575 (all. to his encounter with Abhimanyu); XI, 790 (his corpse is burnt).
Kausalya^2 (C. Kauśº) (do.) = Bṛhadratha: V, 7612 (Bṛhadrathaḥ; read Bṛhadbalaḥ?).
Kausalya^3 (C. Kauśº) (do.) = Vasumanas: XII, 2537 (Vº), 2541, 2595.
Kausalya, pl. (C. Kauśº) (ºāḥ), a people = Kosala, pl. § 608 (Karṇap.): VIII, 47, 2226.
Kausalyā^1 (C. Kauśº), wife of Pūru. § 156 (Pūruvaṃś.): I, 95, ††3764 (mother of Janamejaya^6).
Kausalyā^4 (C. Kauśº), wife of Daśaratha and mother of Rāma. § 525 (Rāmopākhyānap.): III, 274, 15879 (Rāmasya mātā).--§ 527 (do.): III, 277, 15962, 15980.
Kausalyā^5 (C. Kauśº), wife of Janaka. § 624 (Rājadh.): XII, 18, 546.
Kauśija, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 349 (in Bhāratavarsha).

Kauśika^1 (“descendant of Kuśika”) = Viśvāmitra: I, 2936, 6695; III, 8120, 8121 (Vº), 8311 (Vº), 8313; V, 3722, 3728, 3972 (reme…yathā…Haimavatyāñ ca Kºaḥ), 4021, 7354 (ºsyāśrame); IX, 2295, 2384 (ṛshisattamaṃ); XII, 1594(?), 5352, 5353, 5367, 5410, 7599, ††13205(?); XIII, 1350, 2897 (dvijaḥ), 7116 (Vº).
Kauśika^2 (do.) = Ashṭaka: V, 4089 (Aº).
Kauśika^3 (“the son of Kuśika”) = Gādhi: IX, 2297; XIII, 2897.
Kauśika^4 = Caṇḍakauśika: II, 760.
Kauśika^5 = Indra: III, 331, 10312, 10711; XII, 1720 (Gādhir nāma…Pākaśāsanaḥ, incarnate as Gādhi); XIII, 829, 877 (Devarājaḥ), 3590, 3600 (read Kºa with B.), 6950 (ºsya Śacī).

Kauśika,^6 various brahmans, descendants of Kuśika. § 264 (Sabhākriyāp.): II, 4, 107.--§ 277 (Jarāsandhavadhap.): II, 21, 807 (ºo Maṇimāṃś ca, had favoured the country of the Māgadhas, = Caṇḍakauśika?, = Viśvāmitra?).--§ 479 (Pativratop.): III, 206, 13652, 13700.--§ 608g (Karṇap.): An ascetic K. lived near a village where many rivers met. He made a vow always to speak the truth, and became celebrated as a speaker of truth. From fear of robbers, certain persons entered that wood. The robbers came and asked K. by which path the men had gone, and he told them the truth; the robbers finding out the persons slew them all. K. fell into a grievous hell: VIII, 69, 3439, 3446, 3448, 3449, 3451, 3452, 3454.--§ 641 (Rājadh.): XII, 109, 4030 (?Nīl. and PCR. take kauśikaḥ in the sense of ‘an owl’, but this verse seems to allude to VIII, 69, although the text is in disorder).--§ 662b (Jāpakop.): XII, 199, 7201 (Paippalādiḥ sa-Kauśikaḥ).
Kauśika^7, the senāpati of Jarāsandha. § 277 (Jarāsandhavadhap.): II, 22, 885 (formerly named Haṃsa).
Kauśika^8 (III, 8134), v. Kauśikī.

Kauśika, adj. (“relating to Kuśika or Kauśika”). § 435 (Jaṭāsuravadhap.): III, 157, 11461 (khaḍgaṃ).--§ 593 (Abhimanyuvadhap.): VII, 48, 1920 (mārgaiḥ Kºādyaiḥ).-§ 602 (Droṇavadhap.): VII, 191, 8793 (sampātaṃ?).-§ 615 (Gadāyuddhap.): IX, 57, 3223 (mārgān).--§ 745b (Cyavanop.): XIII, 52, 2719 (vaṃśāt).
Kauśika, pl. (ºāḥ) (the descendants of Kuśika or Kauśika). § 225 (Vāsishṭha): I, 176, 6739.
Kaushika = Mahāpurusha (Mahāpurushastava).
Kauśikācārya = Ākṛti: II, 1165 (Āº; read Kaiśº?).

Kauśikī^1, a river. § 134 (Viśvāmitra): I, 71, 2924 (created by Viśvāmitra, who named it Pārā).--§ 249 (Arjunavanavāsap.): I, 215, 7818 (visited by Arjuna).--§ 280 (Bhīmasena): II, 30, 1096 (ºnilayaṃ rājānaṃ Mahaujasaṃ). § 364 (Tīrthayātrāp.): III, 83, 6065 (ºyāḥ…saṅgame …Dṛshadvatyāḥ).--§ 370 (do.): III, 84, 8110, 8121, 8134 (Kālikāsaṅgame…Kºy-Aruṇayor gataḥ, C. has Kauśikāruṇayoḥ).--§ 377 (Dhaumyatīrthak.): III, 87, 8309 (there Viśvāmitra attained to the state of a brahman).--§ 390 (Tīrthayātrāp.): III, 110, 9987 (c: on K. Viśvāmitra practised austerities), 9989.--§ 392 (Tīrthayātrāp.): III, 114, 10095.--§ 459 (Mārkaṇḍeyas.): III, 188, 12907 (seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the stomach of Nārāyaṇa).--§ 494 (Āṅgirasa): III, 222, 14231 (among the rivers who are mothers of fires).--§ 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 326, 337.-§ 594 (Mṛtyu): VII, 54, 2094.--§ 680c (Mṛtyu-Prajāpatisaṃv.): XII, 259, 9207.--§ 721 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 3, 190.--§ 733 (do.): XIII, 25, 1717 (a tīrtha).--§ 751b (Śapathavidhi): XIII, 94, †4552 (puṇyatīrthaṃ).--§ 757m (Goloka): XIII, 101, 4889.--§ 768b (Umā-Maheśvarasaṃv.): XIII, 146, 6764.--§ 775 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 166, 7653 (enumeration). Cf. Pārā.
Kauśikī^2 = Durgā (Umā): VI, 800.
Kausalyāmātṛ (C. Kauśº) (do.) = Rāma Dāśarathi: III, 16302, 16572.
Kausalyānandavardhana (C. Kauśº) (“the son of Kausalyā” [i.e. Ambālikā]) = Pāṇḍu: I, 4466.
Kausalyānandivardhana (C. Kauśº) (“the son of Kausalyā”) = Rāma Dāśarathi: III, 15957.
Kausalyātmajā (C. Kauśº), dual (ºe) = Ambikā and Ambālikā: I, 3804.

Kaustubha, the jewel of Kṛshṇa (Vishṇu). § 28 (Amṛtamanthana): I, 18, 1147 (maṇir divyaḥ, emerged when the gods churned the milky ocean).--§ 521 (Draupadīharaṇap.): III, 263, 15533 (ºbhūshaṇa, sc. Kṛshṇa).--§ 562 (Bhagavadyānap.): V, 94, 3343 (maṇiṃ, worn by Kṛshṇa).-§ 564 (Mātalīyop.): V, 102, 3613 (maṇiratnaṃ, arose at the churning of the [milky]
ocean).--§ 608 (Karṇap.): VIII, 46, 2181 (atyarthaṃ bhrājate Kṛshṇe Kºs tu maṇis tataḥ); 76, †3855 (urasi--sc. Kṛshṇa's--Kºñ ca jājvalyamānaṃ).--§ 637 (Rājadh.): XII, 45, 1546 (ºenorasisthena maṇinābhirājitaṃ, sc. Kṛshṇa). Cf. Kirīṭa-Kaustubhadhara.
